Real case · It actually happened — May 2024

A global superstar “showed up” at the Met Gala — without leaving the house.

During the 2024 Met Gala, hyper-realistic AI photos of Katy Perry on the red carpet went viral and were shared by millions — even though she never set foot there. She was working. She even reposted them: “Couldn't make it to the MET, had to work.”

The wildest part? Her own mother texted her believing the photos were real. And she wasn't alone — AI red-carpet photos of Rihanna and Lady Gaga made the rounds that same night.

If the most photographed people on earth can “attend” an event they skipped — and fool their own families — imagine what the right photo does for a feed nobody's fact-checking. It's a $7 download.

Peer-reviewed research

Better-looking people earn 10–15% more — for the exact same job. Two economists tracked thousands of workers and found a measurable “beauty premium” on every paycheck. Your image isn't decoration — it's priced in.

Hamermesh & Biddle, “Beauty and the Labor Market,” American Economic Review (1994)

People judge you in 100 milliseconds — a tenth of a second, from a single photo. Princeton researchers showed your competence and trustworthiness are decided before you say a word.

Willis & Todorov, “First Impressions,” Psychological Science (2006)

Put those together: the first image people see decides how they judge you — and how much they'll pay you. For about $7, you finally get to choose what that image says.
